summary: NASA has announced $10 billion in moon base contracts and ordered a nuclear-powered lunar rover, alongside launching a $1 million student challenge for lunar base solutions and opening its latest astronaut application window. In deep-space exploration, NASA’s twin ESCAPADE probes are officially en route to Mars after completing an unprecedented double Earth gravity assist, though a separate NASA technology demonstration ended after Starfish Space lost contact with its first Otter servicing spacecraft. In defense space developments, France ordered over €1.5 billion in military Earth-observation satellites, while the U.S. Space Force awarded Viasat a $450 million contract to construct an operations center aimed at harmonizing data networks. Meanwhile, a new Government Accountability Office report revealed the Pentagon cannot track more than one million F-35 spare parts. In international news, Canada confirmed medium-lift rocket ambitions in its national budget. In astrophysics, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory identified the likely source of a giant star's repeated outbursts. Looking ahead, observers should watch for SpaceX's planned Nov. 13 Starship Flight 15 test mission, which is set to attempt a double-catch recovery.
